Monday, Parshat Pinchas,
19th of Tamuz, 5728

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the maamar's opening verse and discusses the connection between the verse "And you shall be strong and become a man" and the Bar Mitzvah celebration, questioning why the term "man" is emphasized at age thirteen.

translations.translation: "And you shall be strong and become a man"¹,
It is known²
that the maamar said by the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory on the seventh day³
of the Bar Mitzvah celebration of his only son, the Rebbe Rayatz,
19th of Tamuz⁴
[This maamar is the conclusion and seal of the series *Tefillin DeMarei Alma*⁵
which he began to say on the 12th of Tamuz,
the day of the Bar Mitzvah]
began with this verse.
– The connection of this verse
("And you shall be strong and become a man")
to Bar Mitzvah on a simple level is,
according to what is known⁶
that a thirteen-year-old
(specifically)
is obligated in mitzvos because only then is he called a man.
And it needs to be understood,
since a thirteen-year-old becomes a man
(by nature),
what is the emphasis in saying
(at the Bar Mitzvah celebration)
"And you shall be strong and become a man."
And also it needs to be understood,
behold, the advantage of a thirteen-year-old is that then he becomes a *baal daas*⁷,
for *daas* is in the intellect,
and particularly according to what is explained in the maamar beginning "It is said in Midrash Tehillim" 5653
[which is one of the maamarim that the Rebbe Rayatz repeated at his Bar Mitzvah celebration]⁸
that the advantage of a thirteen-year-old is that then he has the essence of the intellect⁹,
and what is the precision in a thirteen-year-old regarding the title "man" which indicates¹⁰
about the emotions.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the superiority of Yosef over Yaakov in drawing down revelation into the lower worlds, and analyzes the three levels in the verse "You are Hashem alone" regarding the Ein Sof before the tzimtzum and the constricted line that creates and sustains the worlds.

translations.translation: Now, in the part of the series that was said then¹¹
the superiority of Yosef over Yaakov is explained,
for the drawing down through Yaakov is in Atzilus, while through Yosef the revelation is drawn down
(also)
into Biyah.
[And it can be said,
that this, that in the maamar "And you shall be strong and become a man" it speaks in praise of Yosef,
the first name of the Bar Mitzvah boy,
is also in order to arouse him regarding the unique service of Yosef, to draw down revelation even to the lowest levels].
And in order to explain the greatness of the elevation of Yosef,
it first explains the superiority of Yaakov,
so that through this the greatness of the elevation of Yosef, who is even more elevated, will be understood.
And it explains this by prefacing what is said¹²
"You are Hashem alone; You made the heavens, etc., and You give life to them all,"
which are three levels¹³.
"You are Hashem alone" refers to the Ein Sof before the tzimtzum
[and it details three matters within this,
"You," "He," and "Hashem."
"You" is the essence of the luminary,
and it says about this "You" in the second person,
because the essence is everywhere in revelation¹⁴,
for the name "Heaven" is common in the mouth of everyone.
"He" and "Hashem" are two levels within the light,
the essence of the light
and the diffusion of the light
("Hashem"),
as explained in the maamar.
And it says about this "alone,"
that there is nothing here other than the essence,
for the entirety of the light before the tzimtzum,
even the light that pertains to the worlds
("Hashem"),
is included in His essence and is not in the category of existence¹⁵].
"You made the heavens, etc." is the light as it became a source for the creation of the worlds.
Therefore it is written "You made,"
"made" (את) is missing a *hei*,
because the light,
even the light that pertains to the worlds
("Hashem"),
as it is before the tzimtzum,
is not in a category to be a source for the worlds,
and in order for it to be a source for the worlds it is through the tzimtzum,
that all the light was concealed and only a thin and constricted line was drawn down.
And this is "You made the heavens, etc." "made" (את) missing a *hei*,
that this, that the light became a source for the worlds
("You made the heavens, etc.")
is through it being lacking and diminished
("made" (את) missing a *hei*).
"And You give life to them all" is the line through which life is drawn to the worlds,
after they are created.
That is to say,
that in the line there are two aspects,
it is a thin and constricted line,
and from this aspect it brings the worlds into existence
(the existence of the worlds),
and its drawing down is from the light before the tzimtzum,
and from this aspect it draws down life into the worlds
(revelation of G-dliness)¹⁶.
And this is that "You" here
("And You give life to them all")
is spelled with a full *hei* like the first "You"
("You are Hashem alone"),
because this aspect, that the line gives life to them all,
is from this, that the revelation of the light before the tzimtzum is drawn into it.
